comment: Client 1 (which requests offline_access) successfully exercises the refresh flow; per FAPI2-SP-FINAL 5.3.2.1-9 this AS does not rotate refresh tokens, so the suite's own module logic skips its 'retry with the old token' sub-check for client 1 rather than failing it (FAPI2SPFinalRefreshToken.java logs 'Refresh token not rotated. Skipping lost refresh token test.'). The module then repeats against the plan's second client, which deliberately omits offline_access from its scope, so it gets no refresh token at all and the module reports its overall result as SKIPPED ('Refresh tokens cannot be tested. No refresh token was issued.') - matches the accompanying FAPIEnsureServerConfigurationDoesNotSupportRefreshToken warning in expected-warnings-message-signing.json.

Deterministic, permanent skip: this test requires an RSA client key to sign an RS256 client assertion, and this AS's registered clients only ever use ES256 (see oidf-config/message-signing.config.json and cmd/conformance-as's algorithm policy - no RSA support by design). The suite's own skip message confirms this does not prevent certification.

Same root cause as ensure-signed-client-assertion-with-RS256-fails, applied to request object signing instead of client assertion signing: this test requires an RSA client key to sign an RS256 request object, and this AS's registered clients only ever use ES256. Only reachable under a profile that actually sends signed request objects (message-signing), which is why it doesn't appear in expected-skips-baseline.json.
